## The audit committee's question {#ch19-01 .balanced .stepwise}

Are customer credits and refunds controlled?

Do the balances agree with the records?

What explains the growth in returns?

::: {.notes}
Purpose: introduce the independent audit engagement. Allow 60-90 seconds. The case begins in September 2027, with a report due at the November audit committee meeting. The committee wants evidence on controls and balances together. Teams must decide which queries, external evidence requests, and analytical comparisons answer each question. Misconception to address: an unusual refund proves that someone committed fraud. Pause and ask: What evidence would establish whether a refund was authorized? Transition: define the learning objectives.
:::

## Learning objectives {#ch19-02 .balanced .stepwise}

- Reconcile the cycle and assess its risks.
- Distinguish population tests from evidence that needs sampling.
- Explain returns and investigate refund signals.
- Evaluate deficiencies and design continuing tests.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: identify the capabilities demonstrated by the capstone. Allow 60-90 seconds. The submission should connect each conclusion to an identified population, test, and result. A query can establish a recorded condition, while the investigation may require documents that the database cannot supply. Reporting should preserve that distinction. Misconception to address: testing every database row answers every audit question. Pause and ask: Which control would require evidence outside these tables? Transition: set the dates and scope.
:::

## Scope and dates {#ch19-03 .balanced .stepwise}

Tests cover fiscal 2024-2026.

Control conclusions are as of the end of 2026.

The report goes to the November 2027 meeting.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: separate the transaction window from the reporting date. Allow 60-90 seconds. The data end in 2026 even though fieldwork occurs in 2027. Do not use the meeting date as if it extended the transaction population. The controller, customer service manager, and accounting manager own the cycle and will respond to the findings. Misconception to address: a later report date supplies later transaction evidence. Pause and ask: How would you describe the data cutoff in the report? Transition: organize the working files.
:::

## Working files and handoffs {#ch19-04 .balanced}

| File | Evidence it holds |
|---|---|
| Credits.sql | Reconciliations and document tests |
| Credits Audit.xlsx | Risk matrix, sample, and evaluations |
| Credits Analytics.pbix | Returns analysis and refund ranking |

::: {.notes}
Purpose: assign a clear responsibility to each tool. Allow 60-90 seconds. Run Credits.sql on CharlesRiver_Capstone.sqlite, a working copy of the original download. Export RefundFlags.csv for the analytics report. Update Audit Monitoring.pbix for continuing tests, or create the small register specified by the case if Chapter 16 was not completed. Record source dates and control totals at each handoff. Misconception to address: a visual report replaces the underlying test definition. Pause and ask: How will a reviewer trace a flag back to its query? Transition: sequence the milestones.
:::

## Three milestones {#ch19-05 .balanced .stepwise}

1. Plan the audit: Requirements 1-3.
2. Test controls and balances: Requirements 4-7.
3. Evaluate and report: Requirements 8-10.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: show how the phases depend on each other. Allow 60-90 seconds. Accept the population reconciliations before relying on exception counts. Freeze the sampling plan before interpreting a sample result. Evaluate related deficiencies together before drafting the overall conclusion. Each milestone should leave evidence another team member can reproduce. Misconception to address: the report can be assembled from charts without a documented test plan. Pause and ask: Which planning error could undermine every later conclusion? Transition: map the cycle.
:::

# Milestone 1: plan the audit {#ch19-module-6}

::: {.notes}
Requirements 1 to 3 establish the cycle, reconcile its populations, and document the risks and materiality. Review the evidence boundary before testing.
:::

## A map supported by the records {#ch19-07 .balanced .stepwise}

Trace returns, credits, refunds, and commission adjustments.

Test keys and links with counts and anti-joins.

Mark what each recorded role actually evidences.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: build an observed process map. Allow 60-90 seconds. Follow the document links and retain their grains. Include cash receipts and applications because a refund depends on whether the customer paid. A role recorded in GLEntry may represent approval rather than data entry. The case explicitly warns that CreatedByEmployeeID cannot establish who keyed a credit or refund. Misconception to address: a column name alone establishes the business role it records. Pause and ask: Which control point cannot be evidenced by the recorded employee field? Transition: reconcile the distinct flows.
:::

## Reconciliation needs flows as well as balances {#ch19-08 .balanced .stepwise}

Reconcile each document population by fiscal year.

Explain exclusions, signs, and document dates.

Roll account 2060 forward and identify its open items.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: establish complete populations for subsequent tests. Allow 60-90 seconds. Account 2060 Customer Deposits and Unapplied Cash receives several large flows whose net balance may be small. Reconcile receipts, applications, credits, and refunds separately. Also reconcile returns at standard cost and commission clawbacks, including the required account 2034 year-end balance. Exclude closing entries from the specified income-account reconciliations. Misconception to address: a small ending balance proves that all the flows are correct. Pause and ask: Could two omitted flows offset in a balance check? Transition: make the time definition explicit.
:::

## Each question has a date definition {#ch19-09 .balanced .stepwise}

Posting date follows the source document.

Payment status uses only events known by the refund date.

Returns rates need comparable observation windows.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: prevent future information from entering historical tests. Allow 60-90 seconds. Receipt and deposit dates answer different questions, as do refund date and clearing date. A payment received later cannot justify a refund at an earlier date. Late-2026 shipment cohorts have incomplete return experience, while 2024 has no earlier sales in this dataset. Explain these boundaries in both queries and report labels. Misconception to address: all three fiscal years have equally complete return experience. Pause and ask: Which later event must be excluded from an as-of test? Transition: set case materiality and risk priorities.
:::

## Materiality follows the case instructions {#ch19-10 .balanced .stepwise}

Overall: 5% of recorded 2026 pretax income.

Performance: 75% of overall materiality.

Trivial: 5% of overall materiality.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: state the assignment parameters without supplying the calculated answers. Allow 60-90 seconds. These percentages are requirements of this educational case, not universal audit thresholds. Reconcile the pretax-income base and document the calculation in the workbook. Use the risk assessment to connect magnitude with qualitative concerns, likelihood, and the evidence needed. Misconception to address: a quantitatively small condition cannot matter to control design. Pause and ask: What qualitative feature could require attention below a monetary threshold? Transition: connect risks with testable assertions.
:::

## The risk matrix connects a claim to evidence {#ch19-11 .balanced .stepwise}

Risk and assertion.

Expected control and proposed test.

Database evidence and external evidence still needed.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: turn brainstorming into a test plan. Allow 60-90 seconds. Consider pressure, opportunity, and rationalization when brainstorming fraud risks, then define the recorded condition a query can test. Distinguish a control test from a substantive amount test even when they share one population. Document the tool, expected result, and limitation for each test. Misconception to address: naming a fraud scheme constitutes an audit procedure. Pause and ask: Which assertion does your proposed query actually address? Transition: review the planning milestone.
:::

## Milestone 1 checkpoint {#ch19-12 .balanced .stepwise}

Do the populations reconcile?

Are the date rules and limitations explicit?

Does each significant risk have a test and evidence source?

[Open Requirements 1-3](https://aa.accountinganalyticshub.com/chapters/19-customer-credits-audit/chapter.html#phase-1-plan-the-audit)

::: {.notes}
Purpose: review the basis for fieldwork. Allow 3-5 minutes. Ask teams to demonstrate one two-sided reconciliation and one risk-to-test connection. They should explain the expected result before running the test. Carry unresolved differences visibly, rather than treating them as exceptions from a control that has not yet been tested. Misconception to address: a list of queries is equivalent to a documented audit plan. Pause and ask: What evidence would cause you to revise the plan? Transition: perform the population tests.
:::

# Milestone 2: test controls and balances {#ch19-module-13}

::: {.notes}
Requirements 4 to 7 combine population tests, analytical comparisons, a sampling plan, and document-level substantive work.
:::

## Population tests need stable definitions {#ch19-14 .balanced .stepwise}

Authority and employment at the relevant date.

Separation of approval and cash handling.

Payment, offset, and clawback conditions.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: define reproducible rule populations. Allow 60-90 seconds. Retain the document key and one row per defined condition. Distinguish general Employee authority limits from an external delegation policy. A payment-method difference or missing offset can prompt follow-up without itself proving a breached deterministic rule. Do not infer preparer-versus-approver separation when the preparer is not recorded. Misconception to address: every unusual condition has the same evidential strength. Pause and ask: What additional policy document would settle an authority question? Transition: preserve the flag handoff.
:::

## Refund flags must remain traceable {#ch19-15 .balanced .stepwise}

Keep RefundID and each test label.

Use UNION ALL to preserve distinct failures.

Export RefundFlags.csv with population controls.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: maintain the evidence trail into the report. Allow 60-90 seconds. A refund may fail more than one test. Distinguish the number of failures from the number of refunds with at least one failure, and preserve the year definition used by each count. The report should allow a reviewer to move from a score to the named conditions and underlying documents. Misconception to address: three flags necessarily represent three different refunds. Pause and ask: Which control total detects a duplicated CSV import? Transition: explain returns on comparable bases.
:::

## Returns analysis needs a matching denominator {#ch19-16 .balanced .stepwise}

Compare credit and invoice populations consistently.

Show both credit month and shipment month.

Explain incomplete cohorts and the startup year.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: separate growth from timing and population effects. Allow 60-90 seconds. The requirements ask for rates by year and product grouping, with reasons and other dimensions used to investigate differences. Build the assigned expectation from the 2025 rate and explain why 2024 is a weak base. A chart should identify whether it groups the event of granting a credit or the shipment whose goods were returned. Misconception to address: a higher rate alone establishes the cause of returns. Pause and ask: What happens to a recent shipment cohort as more returns arrive? Transition: rank refunds for investigation.
:::

## A refund score orders follow-up {#ch19-17 .balanced .stepwise}

One point for each defined flag.

Show the individual flags alongside the score.

Drill from refund to credit and invoice.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: use the score as a transparent prioritization device. Allow 60-90 seconds. The assigned score is a count of conditions, not a calibrated probability of fraud. Concentration by customer, approver, carrier, or warehouse also needs an appropriate exposure comparison. Preserve the rule definitions so a reviewer can disagree with a priority without losing the underlying evidence. Misconception to address: a score of three means a threefold fraud risk. Pause and ask: Which flag would require the most urgent external corroboration? Transition: plan tests of unavailable documents.
:::

## Some controls need external documents {#ch19-18 .balanced .stepwise}

Written customer request.

Independent verification of the payee.

Inspection evidence for damaged goods.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: identify the evidence outside the database. Allow 60-90 seconds. These attributes cannot be established from transaction tables alone. The assignment provides no external documents for their execution. Deliver the sampling plan, frozen selection, and evaluation rule, and clearly label the procedures that remain unperformed. Do not invent document inspection results. Misconception to address: absence of a database field proves that a document never existed. Pause and ask: How will the workpaper distinguish planned work from completed work? Transition: design and freeze the sample.
:::

## Sample design precedes selection {#ch19-19 .balanced .stepwise}

Set confidence, tolerable, and expected deviation.

Take the specified key items in full.

Randomly select from the remaining population and freeze it.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: make the selection reproducible. Allow 60-90 seconds. The case takes all refunds of at least $5,000 and customers with more than $10,000 of refunds over the three years as key items. Define the remainder after removing those items. Use the assigned RANDARRAY and SORTBY method, paste the selection as values, and record the date, parameters, and identifiers before examining results. Misconception to address: recalculating a random sample until it looks representative is valid selection. Pause and ask: What record would let another auditor reconstruct your selection population? Transition: write the evaluation rule.
:::

## The evaluation rule is part of the plan {#ch19-20 .balanced .stepwise}

State how deviations change the conclusion.

Compare the upper deviation limit with the tolerable rate.

Test one observable attribute against its whole population.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: connect selection with a predeclared decision rule. Allow 60-90 seconds. Use the assigned sampling table and the book's BETA.INV procedure for the required hypothetical deviation counts, observing its domain and edge cases. The observable-attribute comparison demonstrates sampling uncertainty using a known population result. It does not supply results for unavailable customer documents. Misconception to address: a sample with no observed deviations proves a zero population deviation rate. Pause and ask: What would make the planned reliance inappropriate? Transition: test amounts and event sequences.
:::

## Substantive tests follow the document chain {#ch19-21 .balanced .stepwise}

Recompute quantities, prices, discounts, and related amounts.

Test cumulative credits against the invoice.

Explain open balances and returned-goods valuation.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: test recorded amounts independently of the approval checks. Allow 60-90 seconds. The public requirement specifies the tax, freight, commission, inventory, and credit computations. An approval can exist while an amount is wrong. Preserve line-level keys and aggregate before joining populations that could multiply one another. Explain unresolved items in account 2060 at the required date. Misconception to address: an authorized credit is necessarily accurate. Pause and ask: Which amount must be tested cumulatively rather than document by document? Transition: construct the timeline evidence.
:::

## A timeline separates observations from explanations {#ch19-22 .balanced .stepwise}

Order receipt, application, return, credit, and refund events.

Identify the recorded people and dates.

List the external evidence needed to resolve the pattern.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: investigate without overstating the evidence. Allow 60-90 seconds. The case asks for a timeline of the largest refund and for tests of lapping indicators. Students identify the document themselves. Distinguish a date gap from a demonstrated cause. Explain why a first-digit test may be unsuitable for a constrained or selected population rather than running it automatically. Misconception to address: an unusual sequence establishes intent. Pause and ask: Which competing explanation would your evidence request distinguish? Transition: review the fieldwork milestone.
:::

## Milestone 2 checkpoint {#ch19-23 .balanced .stepwise}

Can every exception be traced and reproduced?

Are sample selection and evaluation rules frozen?

Are unperformed external procedures labeled?

[Open Requirements 4-7](https://aa.accountinganalyticshub.com/chapters/19-customer-credits-audit/chapter.html#phase-2-test-controls-and-balances)

::: {.notes}
Purpose: review evidence quality before rating findings. Allow 3-5 minutes. Ask teams to show one rule definition, one analytical qualification, and the boundary of one external procedure. Reconcile the exception populations back to the accepted planning totals. A missing document result is a scope limitation, not a blank to fill with an assumed answer. Misconception to address: more tests necessarily produce stronger evidence. Pause and ask: What conclusion is supported now, and what remains unresolved? Transition: evaluate the findings.
:::

# Milestone 3: evaluate and report {#ch19-module-24}

::: {.notes}
Requirements 8 to 10 evaluate related deficiencies, communicate to the committee, and define the tests that will continue after the engagement.
:::

## Severity requires a reasoned evaluation {#ch19-25 .balanced .stepwise}

Distinguish design from operation.

Assess likelihood and potential magnitude.

Evaluate compensating controls and related deficiencies.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: connect the condition to a supported severity judgment. Allow 60-90 seconds. Explain whether a compensating control is precise enough to address the risk and what evidence shows it operates. Aggregate related conditions that affect the same account or assertion. The amount of one observed exception does not necessarily bound the potential exposure. Apply the assigned control-evaluation guidance with its scope stated. Misconception to address: a control with a different name automatically compensates for the weakness. Pause and ask: What evidence would change your severity judgment? Transition: write the committee finding.
:::

## A finding has an evidence trail {#ch19-26 .balanced .stepwise}

Condition and criteria.

Supported cause and effect.

Rating, recommendation, owner, and proposed date.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: write a finding that a decision maker can evaluate. Allow 60-90 seconds. Use wording about recorded conditions rather than accusations. If the cause is not established, say what needs investigation. Management owns its response, so distinguish proposed action plans from responses actually obtained. Include clean results with their scope and limitations as well as exceptions. Misconception to address: a drafted action plan proves management agreed to implement it. Pause and ask: Which sentence in the finding is observation, and which is judgment? Transition: organize the committee report.
:::

## The committee report is selective {#ch19-27 .balanced .stepwise}

At most three pages of report.

At most three pages of exhibits.

Overall conclusion, scope, significant findings, and actions.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: prioritize a concise committee communication. Allow 60-90 seconds. The case limits the report and its exhibits separately. Use the exhibits for the most useful reconciliations and comparisons rather than every query output. State disagreements and unresolved evidence accurately, and preserve detailed workpapers outside the short report. Misconception to address: a concise report should omit material scope limitations. Pause and ask: Which exhibit most directly supports the overall conclusion? Transition: define continuing tests.
:::

## Four rules enter continuing monitoring {#ch19-28 .balanced .stepwise}

Credit above authority.

Credit approver handled the customer's cash.

Refund above authority.

Refund before customer payment.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: implement the assigned deterministic monitoring scope. Allow 60-90 seconds. Add the credit-memo and refund populations to the register with stable test identifiers and document keys. The requirement keeps payment-method mismatches and missing offsets as anomaly tests outside this deterministic register. Document each denominator and as-of rule. If Chapter 16 is unavailable, build the smaller register described by the case. Misconception to address: every investigative signal belongs in the same rule-failure count. Pause and ask: What identifier will keep a disposition attached after refresh? Transition: preserve history after remediation.
:::

## A fix date changes the review population {#ch19-29 .balanced .stepwise}

Keep historical findings and dispositions.

Record the remediation date and rule version.

Review new exceptions after the fix.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: make monitoring useful after a design finding. Allow 60-90 seconds. Use one coherent treatment for historical failures so an unchanged history does not repeatedly flood the open queue. Preserve the record rather than deleting it, and test new activity after the agreed change. Document source coverage and rule changes so a lower count cannot conceal a narrower population. Misconception to address: a falling exception count alone proves remediation worked. Pause and ask: What evidence would demonstrate that the new control operated? Transition: complete the handoff.
:::

## Final submission checkpoint {#ch19-30 .balanced .stepwise}

Queries, reconciliations, and documented definitions.

Workbook, frozen sample, and evaluation rules.

Analytics report, committee report, and continuing tests.

[Open the deliverables checklist](https://aa.accountinganalyticshub.com/chapters/19-customer-credits-audit/chapter.html#deliverables-and-checklist)

::: {.notes}
Purpose: check that another auditor can follow the work. Allow 3-5 minutes. Review the public deliverables checklist line by line. Verify the links between query results, the CSV, workbook evaluations, and report exhibits. Each conclusion should retain its evidence boundary, and any external work not performed should remain clearly identified. Misconception to address: an attractive final report completes undocumented workpapers. Pause and ask: Could another team reproduce the conclusion from your submission? Transition: acknowledge the conceptual sources.
:::
